title: Four days into the alpha: I moved my tiny-car racing game to Godot and added three tracks. Can you guess the real circuits?
author: ManureTaster
selftext:
I've been building Speedorama, a small racing game where tiny cars race around tabletop dioramas: a breakfast table, a billiard table, a workbench. It's free and runs in the browser. 

Four days ago I put an early alpha online, and a few things happened since.

The game now runs on Godot. I ported it over, and it feels nicer to work with and to look at.

There are three new big tracks:

Shogun's Garden: a Japanese zen garden with red torii gates, bridges and cherry blossoms.

Titan's Peak: a mythological landscape with a bronze Titan, a river and the occasional lightning bolt.

Corkscrew Canyon: a dry California hillside with a steep drop that your tiny car will have opinions about.

Each of them is a miniature replica of a real, famous racing circuit, traced from real map data! It's a different take compared to the smaller, snappier circuits.

A few numbers from the first four days, which made me smile:

About 210 visitors from 33 countries, of whom 76 actually drove a race.

129 races started, and 82% of them were on the breakfast table. The new tracks are feeling a bit shy, so I'm hoping you'll go and meet them.

You can play solo against bots, or with friends using their phones as controllers. 

I'd love to hear your feedback!

https://stegodon.games/play/speedorama
